sentences.text: This appeal is filed by the third respondent, insurer of the offending vehicle, in O.P (MV) No.442 of 2015 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Taliparamba, challenging the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal and the locus standi of the claimant in filing the claim petition.
The respondent herein is the claimant before the Tribunal.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows: On 24.03.2012 at about 10.30 p.m., while the deceased was travelling in a motorcycle bearing registration No.KL-13-W-4062 from Taliparamba to Sreekandapuram, a car bearing registration No.KL-60-D-2412 driven by the second respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit against the motorcycle and as a result, the deceased sustained serious injuries and succumbed to the injuries on 27.03.2012 while undergoing treatment.
The deceased was a priest belonging to the Diocese of Kannur.
The claimant, 2025:KER:66467 MACA NO. 4074 OF 2016 the Diocese of Kannur, represented by its Procurator, approached the Tribunal claiming a total compensation of 10,00,000/-.

3. Though notice was served on the respondents, the first and second respondents, the owner and the driver of the offending vehicle respectively did not appear and remained ex parte before the Tribunal.
The third respondent - insurer filed a written statement, admitting the insurance policy and disputing the liability and quantum of compensation claimed.
They contended that the petitioner is not the legal heir of the deceased and the petitioner has no locus standi to file the claim petition.
It was specifically contended that the legal heirs alone are entitled for the compensation.
Before the Tribunal, Exts.A1 to A4 were marked.

The Tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, found that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the second respondent and awarded a sum of 7,78,800/- as compensation under different heads with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of petition till realization with proportionate 2025:KER:66467 MACA NO. 4074 OF 2016 costs against the third respondent being the insurer.
Challenging the award passed, the third respondent insurance company has come up in appeal.
4. Though notice was served on the respondent he chose not to appear before this court.
I have heard the learned standing counsel for the appellant, insurance company.

5. The learned standing counsel for the insurer submitted that the claimant was not a legal heir to file a petition claiming compensation for the death of the deceased who was a priest attached to the Diocese of Kannur.

The learned Standing Counsel appearing for the insurance company also relied on the judgment of this Court in Catholic Diocese, Muvattupuzha and others v. Muthaiah P. And Another [2019 (4) KHC 865], wherein it was held that a Catholic Diocese is not entitled to claim compensation for the death of a deceased priest and that only the siblings of the priest can be considered his legal representatives for the purpose of raising a claim for compensation.

entities.text: Catholic Diocese, Muvattupuzha and others v. Muthaiah P. And Another [2019 (4) KHC 865]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The insurer also relied on the 2025:KER:66467 MACA NO. 4074 OF 2016 Apex Court judgments in Molly Joseph v. George Sebastian [1997 KHC 1] and Mary Roy v. State of Kerala [1986 KHC 129] which held that the inheritance or succession to Christians shall only be in terms of the succession act and hence the legal heirs of the deceased are only entitled to claim compensation and therefore, not the claim petitioner herein.

sentences.text: On a perusal of the award dated 10.12.2015, in O.P. (MV) No. 442/2015 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Taliparamba, it is clear that the deceased was a priest attached to the Diocese of Kannur.
It is also seen that the legal heirs of the deceased were not impleaded in the party array.
The accident and the death are admitted.

7. In the present case, neither the legal representatives nor the legal heirs of the deceased priest were impleaded as parties to the proceedings and the claim petition was filed solely by the Diocese of Kannur.

Hence, following the judgment in Muthaiah (supra), I hold that the siblings of the deceased priest alone can be 2025:KER:66467 MACA NO. 4074 OF 2016 regarded as his legal representatives for the purpose of raising a claim for compensation.
Accordingly, the award passed by the Tribunal granting compensation to the claim petitioner /respondent is against law and is not sustainable.

Considering the afore facts, the appeal is allowed and the award dated 10.12.2015 in O.P.(MV)
No.442/2015 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Thaliparamba is set aside.

It is made clear that the insurance company will be at liberty to claim refund of the compensation amount deposited before the Tribunal, pursuant to the interim order passed by this Court on 27.07.2017.

Sd/-
SHOBA ANNAMMA EAPEN JUDGE RK National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Diocese Of Kannur
